body:
FAST-FOLLOW TO T263. Myk's merge: this ticket formalizes an architectural boundary and changes the path future features are expected to take. It does not reopen T263's container-policy decisions and it does not greenfield Loam.

THE PROBLEM.

Loam was originally organized around one Gateway, its primary ground, and an operator whose authority was broad enough to act as the default author of constitutional changes. Containers, channel pools and connection inboxes later made the actual model recursive: an operation occurs from a position, over selected grounds, within a container scope, under a particular signer and law set.

The code now contains both models.

The old model remains in helpers and doors that answer an omitted position by silently choosing the Gateway's primary Reactor, the store-wide materialization, or the operator signer. The new model explicitly constructs a bound ground or container scope. Both may produce correct results today, but the easiest precedent for a coding agent to copy is often the ambient-root one. As container-local law and standing land in T263, that becomes a continuing source of mild incoherence: data is correctly routed to an inbox while an adjacent read, registration, subscription, renderer or administrative gesture silently consults or writes the primary ground.

THE PRINCIPLE.

Ground and operator remain real. They cease to be ambient.

The ground is the physical and constitutional root of one store: it holds store-wide claims and the declarations from which containers are resolved. The operator is a signer with broad standing and responsibility for bootstrap/root administration. Neither word is deprecated, and neither is to be mechanically renamed merely for existing.

What is deprecated is the unmarked assumption that: "ground" means the whole world relevant to the current operation; an omitted scope means the primary Reactor; authority to request an operation means the operator should author its result; law belongs in primary unless a caller remembers to choose otherwise; a root materialization is suitable for a bound, pooled, historical or container-scoped read; a missing context may be repaired by constructing the root context inside the callee.

A read is always from a position. A write is always by a signer into a named ground. An administrative act may authorize, expose, adopt or reassert another peer's claims, but those are separate acts and must not collapse into an implicit operator signature.

THE SIX RULES.

R1 - NO VIEW FROM NOWHERE. Every ordinary query, mutation, registration, subscription, renderer preparation, listing and federation operation receives or derives an explicit context naming the grounds, container scope, law sources, time posture and requesting identity that govern the operation. Root is one explicit context, never the answer to an omitted one.

R2 - AUTHORITY IS NOT AUTHORSHIP. The right to request an operation, the ground into which its result lands, the signer of the resulting delta, and the readers that accept it are separate decisions. Code must not translate "this actor has standing" into "sign an equivalent claim as the operator" unless the operation is explicitly a root reassertion/adoption act.

R3 - ROOT POWER REQUIRES A NAMED CAPABILITY. Generic Gateway and surface code cannot reach the operator seed or raw root Reactor merely because both exist on the Gateway. Bootstrap, genesis and explicitly root-administrative paths receive a narrow root capability. Constructing or passing that capability is visible at the call site.

R4 - CONTEXT IS A TYPE, NOT AN OPTIONS BAG. The new boundary must not be one interface full of optional `actor?`, `container?`, `ground?`, `asOf?` fields whose missing values recreate today's defaults. P1 decides the exact type split, beginning from separate read, write and root-administration capabilities. An invalid combination should be unrepresentable where practical and refused at one named construction boundary otherwise.

R5 - COMPATIBILITY CONFESSES ITSELF. Any ambient-root path that must remain temporarily is centralized and carries the literal `legacy_` marker in its internal filename or symbol. Each retained path is listed in the seam manifest with its reason, replacement and deletion condition. An agent searching `legacy_` can see the entire known compatibility surface. New production code may not import or call it outside the manifest's allowlisted adapters. Public package compatibility is not silently broken to obtain the spelling. Existing exported APIs may remain as deprecated wrappers for the compatibility period P1 chooses, but they delegate immediately into a manifest-listed `legacy_` adapter and may not contain an independent implementation.

R6 - THE CENSUS RATCHETS CLOSED. The audit is a delivered, machine-checked artifact, not a list in a PR description. Every direct access to operator signing material, the raw primary Reactor/ground, implicit-root gathering or root-default context construction is classified. Adding a new site fails CI until the manifest is deliberately widened and the architecture review is routed.

USER STORIES FOR P1.

(1) A maintainer adds a new container-scoped operation. Its implementation cannot compile or pass the seam guard until it receives an explicit context. The maintainer never needs to remember that a particular Gateway helper defaults to primary.
(2) A coding agent encounters an old root-default call. The literal `legacy_` name and its manifest entry state why it exists, what replaces it, and what event permits its removal. Copying that call into an ordinary module makes the guard red.
(3) An operator uses the existing root-level CLI and HTTP surfaces after the migration. Their observable behavior is unchanged, but the boundary constructs an explicit root-administrative or root-read context before entering Gateway logic.
(4) A connection bound beneath `ada:journal` registers law, writes data and reads it after T263. All three operations use the same container position. No generic helper re-signs its registration into primary or resolves its read against the root materialization.
(5) A receiver adopts or reasserts foreign law. The arriving peer claim, the local adoption decision and any locally reasserted claim remain separate and separately attributable. Merely having permission to invoke the operation never changes the peer's author into the operator.
(6) A package consumer using a pre-ticket root-default API receives a documented compatibility path for the P1-decided period. New code is directed to the explicit API. Compatibility does not preserve an unmarked internal back door.

DELIVERABLE 1 - THE WORKING SPEC. P1 produces `.adlc/specs/59-explicit-context.md`, opening with the stories above in observable terms and then defining: what a read context must carry; what a write target must carry; what a root-administrative capability permits; where contexts are constructed; which operations are irreducibly root-level; how public compatibility is handled; the literal `legacy_` naming rule; the manifest schema and enforcement boundary; the incremental migration order; the behavior-preservation promise.

The P1 interrogation must explicitly decide: (a) whether read, write and administration are three types or another capability-safe split; (b) which current exported Gateway methods are public compatibility obligations; (c) the compatibility duration and removal signal for those exports; (d) which operations are irreducibly root-level after T263; (e) whether context carries resolved ground handles, declarative coordinates from which handles are resolved, or a split of both; (f) how subscriptions and historical/pinned reads represent a scope they cannot yet execute - an honest typed refusal is acceptable, an implicit root fallback is not; (g) whether the manifest guard uses the TypeScript compiler API, a lexical tripwire, or both, including an explicit account of what it cannot detect.

Then STOP for Myk's explicit approval before implementation. The landing writes `spec/59-explicit-context.md`; the working spec is the P1 instrument and does not enter `spec/` early.

DELIVERABLE 2 - THE AMBIENT-AUTHORITY CENSUS. Walk every production use of: operator seed/signing material; operator identity used as a substitute author; `gateway.reactor`, `_reactor`, raw primary snapshots and root materializations; methods whose omitted ground/scope selects primary; direct append into primary; registration or adoption paths that operator-sign on another actor's request; bound/channel/container helpers that fall back to root; doors that reconstruct a partial context independently; replay code that aggregates only a hard-coded subset of attached grounds; exported APIs that preserve ambient-root behavior.

Record every occurrence in `scripts/root-authority-seam.json`. Each entry carries at least: file and symbol/site; classification (`bootstrap`, `explicit-root`, `boundary-adapter`, `legacy`, or `defect`); why root/operator access is legitimate or accidental; replacement API/context; whether it is permanent; deletion condition when temporary.

No occurrence may remain unclassified. A site that fits no category is a finding: either the boundary is incomplete or the code is wrong. The census happens before mass renaming. A name is not evidence that its semantics were understood.

DELIVERABLE 3 - THE SEAM MANIFEST AND GUARD. `scripts/root-authority-seam-guard.mjs` makes the census a ratchet. It must: report new unmanifested access to the known raw capabilities; report a missing manifest entry for any literal `legacy_` production symbol; report use of a `legacy_` symbol outside its declared compatibility adapters; report manifest entries whose named file/symbol no longer exists; report permanent entries incorrectly marked `legacy`; report temporary legacy entries without a replacement and deletion condition; exit nonzero on violations; say in its output that it is a tripwire over named syntactic capabilities, not proof that no ambient authority can exist.

The detector's vocabulary and blind spots are written in section 59. It may use the repository's TypeScript compiler API; it must not add a large parsing dependency merely to perform this census. If a lexical floor remains useful, it supplements rather than impersonates semantic proof. The guard's own rail demonstrates red with a planted violation. A detector only observed green has proved nothing. The manifest carries explicit expected-member or minimum-count floors so deleting the detector's vocabulary or emptying the manifest cannot manufacture a green bar. A diff touching the manifest, guard, a raw-capability provider, or a `legacy_` adapter routes an architecture/authority review through `scripts/p5-triage.mjs`.

DELIVERABLE 4 - EXPLICIT CONTEXT CONSTRUCTION. Introduce the P1-approved context/capability types and one named construction layer. The shape starts from these semantic components, without committing P1 to these exact TypeScript names: requesting actor and actual delta signer; write target Gateway/ground; contributing read grounds; container/subtree scope; source of schema/registration law; trust and negation closure; present or `asOf` posture; connection/channel binding where applicable; attachment/lifecycle guarantees; optional explicit root-administrative capability.

Context construction resolves and validates these components once. Individual query, renderer, subscription and mutation paths do not independently rediscover them. There is no optional-context overload that falls back to root. Root boundaries call an explicitly named root constructor.

DELIVERABLE 5 - QUARANTINE THE LEGACY SURFACE. After the census and context types exist: rename confirmed temporary internal ambient paths with a literal `legacy_` marker; move them behind the smallest practical compatibility module or modules; preserve attribution to their callers (a wrapper must not become a place where everything is operator-signed); mark public compatibility wrappers deprecated and route them immediately through the manifest-listed adapter; prevent new internal callers mechanically; remove any wrapper whose only caller can be migrated in the same readable change.

Do not rename legitimate root concepts. `ground`, `operator`, `genesis`, root container declarations and explicit root-administrative operations keep accurate names.

DELIVERABLE 6 - MIGRATE THE DOORS. Every production surface is classified and migrated: GraphQL query and mutation; REST/OpenAPI query and mutation; subscriptions; `asOf` and version-pinned reads; renderer preparation and execution; listing and byte/accounting reads; schema registration; law/data adoption and promotion; federation channels and offers; connection-bound MCP tools; CLI and browser entry points.

For each surface, one of three outcomes is permitted: it consumes the common explicit context; it constructs an explicit root context at a named external boundary; or it refuses a context it cannot honestly support, with the limitation named and tracked. Implicit primary-ground fallback is not a fourth outcome.

NON-GOALS. Do not remove the ground or operator concepts. Do not redesign T263's leeway or derived-standing policy. Do not implement section 58 S3-S7. Do not alter Rhizomatic delta bytes or invent a migration unless P1 finds an unavoidable wire change. Do not combine exposure, adoption, reassertion and authorship into one promotion operation. Do not rewrite Gateway or the repository from scratch. Do not use a mass rename as a substitute for the census. Do not make every operation generic across arbitrary contexts if its honest domain is narrower. Do not weaken, rewrite or predeclare nonexistent rails to make the migration green. Do not change observable root behavior in a mechanics PR - a desired behavior change becomes its own decision-bearing slice.

Acceptance criteria:
- (1) THE CENSUS IS COMPLETE AND MACHINE-READABLE. Every direct production access to the raw operator signer, raw root Reactor/ground, implicit-root gather and known root-default helper is represented in `scripts/root-authority-seam.json`, classified and tied to a replacement or permanent justification. The test carries an expected-member/floor defense against an emptied list. Verify: test/scripts/root-authority-seam.test.ts and `node scripts/root-authority-seam-guard.mjs`.
- (2) THE GUARD HAS BEEN SEEN RED. A planted unmanifested raw-root access fails; a planted `legacy_` call outside its adapter fails; a stale manifest row fails; and the unchanged classified tree passes. Verify: test/scripts/root-authority-seam-guard.test.ts.
- (3) ROOT IS EXPLICIT. An ordinary Gateway operation cannot omit its context and reach primary. Root CLI/HTTP entry points construct an explicit root context, and their existing observable behavior remains unchanged. Verify: test/gateway/context-boundary.test.ts and `npm run check`.
- (4) CONTEXT HAS NO AMBIENT DEFAULT. Missing actor, write target, scope or law source cannot be repaired inside an ordinary operation by selecting the Gateway's defaults. The negative compile/runtime fixtures fail at the construction boundary and a complete explicit context succeeds. Verify: test/types/context-boundary.test.ts and test/gateway/context-boundary.test.ts.
- (5) AUTHORIZATION DOES NOT CHANGE THE AUTHOR. After T263, a connection registering beneath `ada:journal` produces connection-authored law in its inbox pool; no equivalent operator-authored registration appears in primary. A separate explicit root adoption/reassertion produces its own separately attributable claim. Assert both the deltas/bytes and the served object/door result. Verify: test/server/context-boundary.test.ts.
- (6) ONE POSITION GOVERNS THE CONNECTION'S OPERATIONS. A bound connection's query, mutation and registration all resolve from the same container position. None lands in or reads through primary merely because a shared helper was called. A sibling and parent remain unreachable; an operator's explicit root read remains unchanged. Verify: test/server/context-boundary.test.ts.
- (7) EVERY DOOR IS ACCOUNTED FOR. Query, mutation, subscription, pinned/as-of read, renderer, listing, registration, adoption and federation appear in a hand-written expected table stating explicit-context, explicit-root or honest-refusal. Removing a door from the accounting makes the test red. Verify: test/gateway/context-door-census.test.ts.
- (8) LEGACY IS SEARCHABLE AND CLOSED. Every retained internal compatibility symbol contains literal `legacy_`, appears in the manifest, names a replacement and deletion condition, and is imported only from its allowed adapter. A new use fails the guard. Legitimate permanent root operations contain no misleading legacy marker. Verify: test/scripts/root-authority-seam.test.ts and `node scripts/root-authority-seam-guard.mjs`.
- (9) PUBLIC COMPATIBILITY IS DELIBERATE. Every P1-designated exported root-default API either has been migrated through a documented explicit replacement or survives as a deprecated compatibility wrapper for the decided interval. The wrapper delegates; replacing its body with an independent ambient implementation makes a named test fail. Verify: test/gateway/public-context-compat.test.ts and `npm run typecheck`.
- (10) THE MANIFEST ROUTES REVIEW. Touching a raw-capability provider, the manifest, guard or legacy adapter causes `scripts/p5-triage.mjs` to select the authority/context lens; an unrelated source change does not. A missing or malformed manifest fails closed. Verify: test/scripts/p5-context-triage.test.ts.
- (11) NO WIRE MIGRATION IS SMUGGLED IN. The migration changes call structure and explicit context, not existing delta encodings. A pre-ticket store opens and reads identically through an explicit root context. If any delta shape changes, this criterion fails and a section 20 migration must be designed explicitly. Verify: test/gateway/context-backcompat.test.ts.
- (12) THE REFACTOR PRESERVES BEHAVIOR EXCEPT WHERE THE SPEC NAMES A DEFECT. Capture representative root, container-bound and channel-bound behavior before the first migration slice and compare it after each slice. Any difference not named in section 59 becomes a separate ticket rather than being absorbed as cleanup. Verify: recorded `adlc behavior-diff` evidence plus the story rails above.

P2 DECOMPOSITION IS MANDATORY. This is an architectural parent ticket and must not become one unreadable pull request. After P1 approval, P2 decomposes it into independently mergeable slices with explicit contracts. Recommended starting sequence: (1) census only, classify current sites and change no runtime behavior; (2) manifest, guard and P5 routing over the unchanged baseline; (3) context/capability types and explicit root constructors, with temporary legacy adapters; (4) read-side migration - query, historical reads, subscriptions, renderers and listings; (5) write/law migration - mutation, registration, adoption and federation; (6) external-boundary migration - HTTP, MCP, CLI and browser entry points; (7) legacy contraction - remove migrated adapters, tighten the manifest and land section 59.

Slices 4 and 5 may proceed independently only if P2 proves they do not both churn Gateway's same ownership surface. Otherwise they remain sequential. Every slice must merge usefully and preserve the preceding slice's rails unchanged.

RAILS ARE EMPTY AT P0 BY DESIGN. The paths above are proposed verification scope, not frozen rails. Per Loam's standing ADLC rule, declare each rail with `adlc ticket update` only after the test exists, has been copied onto the base tree, and its claimed red behavior has been measured. Controls that legitimately pass on the base identify themselves as controls and do not pad the red count.

CARE. This ticket changes the architectural route by which future authority-bearing work is built. It is not a repair-only self-merge. P1 and the final section 59 landing require Myk's explicit approval; P6 is Myk's merge.

The first P1 sentence must preserve the distinction that motivated the ticket: Ground and operator are not legacy. Ambient ground and ambient operator authority are.

OPEN, PENDING MYK'S RULING (Claude, 2026-09-03): the T263 -> T274 edge is NOT wired yet, because the dependency may run the other way for one slice. Criterion (5) requires connection-authored law in the inbox pool, and T263's registration slice CANNOT produce that: src/gateway/lifecycle.ts:872 refuses any seed whose author is not the operator ("only the operator may publish a registration"), and its own comment gives the reason - "a governed store binds only the OPERATOR's law (readRegistrations filters on it)". The section 47 inbox fold added on branch t263-pr3-derived-standing filters on operatorAuthor for the same reason. So T263 PR 3 works only because the operator signs a connection's law, and passing the context correctly would BREAK it rather than fix it. R2's authorship slice is therefore a prerequisite of T263's registration slice, not a follow-on to it. Wire the edge once Myk rules on the order.
title: SPEC 59 - Make ground and operator explicit, never ambient
